intent: !has(aString) || aString == "one": absence or a value, so the has() is not a guard and stays in the plan.

plannerDivergence.issue: has() over an omitted attribute: unknown to the planner, absent to check()
plannerDivergence.reason: Before 0.57.0 the planner folds has() to true, so the plan is eq(aString, "one") alone. The per-row check() call sends j1's omitted aString as absent, so !has() is true and check() allows j1. From 0.57.0 the plan carries the has().

trap: j1 lacks aString and is allowed by the !has(); dropping the has() as a guard, or folding it like an AND guard, denies j1.
